title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 4 Jul to 14 Sep 2026
summary: From 4 Jul to 14 Sep 2026 the radar shows the lake shrinking from 31.86 km2 to 30.17 km2, a change of -5.3%. HH over the land rose by 0.44 dB on average across the 72 days.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: The lake lost 1.69 km2. In HH, 2.8 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.28 km2 darker. Mean HV moved by -0.09 dB, with 0.64 km2 brighter and 0.47 km2 darker in HV.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: Rough dry ground and fields had 1.03 km2 brighter in HH, rising 0.5 dB. The open water type had 0.64 km2 brighter in HH, which fits a shoreline that moved. The changing fields type rose 1.16 dB in HV and 1.24 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the lake: summer drawdown; the dam's records would confirm it. Possible cause for the brighter shore: ground left dry by falling water echoes more than water does. Possible cause for the changing fields: crops growing on a few plots; a field visit would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. Lake areas are approximate: 12.7% and 9.7% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Compare the 1.69 km2 loss with the dam's level change over the same 72 days. Map the shore segments that turned brighter to see where the water retreated.
